The only fee on record is $5.00, which is the waiting-time fee amount, not the $6.61 cancellation fee, so the charge can only be sustained through NS-6, which requires that the rider boarded and the trip was completed — the driver cancelled and never carried the rider, so no $5.00 was chargeable.

A waiting-time fee under NS-6 additionally requires the driver to tap the $5.00 waiting-fee button at drop-off inside a completed trip; the record shows no completed trip and no such tap, only the cancellation, so the fee is not made out and must be waived.

The chat shows the driver was already at the pickup at 12:17 ("At the pickup now, white Honda Vezel") and that as late as 12:25 the rider had not been marked as a no-show on the app until the driver's own message "8 min up, cancelling the trip", so the rider was given no usable opportunity to board before cancellation.
NS-2 applies in the alternative: if any NS-1 element fails, the rider bears no charge at all and the amount taken must be refunded in full; here the charge is $5.00, so $5.00 falls to be returned.

The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days against 824 trips and 3 disputes, so if the panel finds the cancellation charge was not properly made out, an account review flag is justified as a repeated pattern — this profile fact only supports the extra action and does not decide the case.

weaknesses: The system records cut against me on the core no-show test: F6 shows the driver tapped "I'm Here" 39 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 8 min 10 s afterwards, and F2/F3 show 9 min 35 s cumulative within 200 m with the driver stationary 41 m away for 8 min 30 s — on NS-1's default reading (and even more so on an 8-minute case threshold) the driver's wait looks compliant, so my complaint that he cancelled too early is weak.

The driver's written statement (F12) expressly claims he pressed "I'm Here" and waited the full 8 minutes; although F12 is a mere statement and F9–F11 show the chat record is complete, the panel may find the driver's account consistent with the GPS, which undercuts C4.

My client produced no in-app message, so there is no evidence in the chat (F9–F11) of what time she actually came out; the complaint's timing assertion rests on her own narrative alone and will be tested against F1/F2/F3/F5, and no GPS or timeline fact records the rider arriving at the pickup point.
The rider's own profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days (F16) with 0 upheld, which the other side may use to suggest a habit of disputing fees; it is minor but it is on the record.

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:17:10, and the GPS timeline places him within 200 m of the pickup point at that moment (39 m), satisfying the arrival/position requirement of NS-1(i)-(ii); the arrival had also already been recorded by the platform at 12:15:25 (F5).

After the "I'm Here" tap the driver remained inside the 200 m pickup radius for 8 min 10 s and only cancelled 9 min 55 s after recorded arrival, so the continuous-wait requirement (more than 3 minutes) and the recorded 8-minute no-show threshold were both met (F6, F5, F4); under NS-1 the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee therefore stands.

The GPS track shows the driver stationary at 41 m from the pickup point from 12:16:50 until the cancellation at 12:25:20 (8 min 30 s), with a closest approach of 6 m at 12:16:45 — he was physically waiting at the pickup point, not elsewhere (F3, F1).

Chat #1 at 12:17 ("At the pickup now, white Honda Vezel") is time-stamped and shows the driver notified the rider of his presence and vehicle at the pickup point from the very start of the wait, and Chat #2 at 12:25 ("8 min up, cancelling the trip") shows he warned the rider before cancelling; the chat record is complete with 2 timestamped messages, so there is no G12 gap that would force escalation (F9, F10, F11).

The rider was billed $5.00 (not $6.61) and the trip shows no surge (1.0×), so no inflated or unpublished item is in issue and the charge is confined to the recorded no-show cancellation fee; no FARE-1 excess exists to refund (F7, F8, F4).

Route and traffic records show no incident on the route during the trip window and light traffic (band 3, 20–29 km/h) with fair weather, i.e. the driver's decision to wait and then cancel was not masking any route deviation or unsafe conduct on his part (F13, F14, F15).

The driver's profile (3.2-year account, 824 trips/90 d, 4.66 rating) shows a high-volume long-tenure record; the 2 previously upheld no-show disputes (F17) are the rider's allegations, and since the driver's cancellation here is NS-1-compliant the case should not be escalated to an account flag on this record alone.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint ("by the time I came out he had cancelled") is a statement that no GPS/timeline record directly contradicts on its face — the record shows the driver waited 9 min 55 s, but the rider will argue that is still a short wait against her perception of the pickup point (her statement goes to F4/F5).

G2: Ryde has not published the metre radius for "at the pick-up location according to GPS data"; the 200 m figure is a data-layer parameter, so the rider may argue the tap at 39 m from the pickup (F6) was not "at" the point, and the policy notes the exact radius is an open item.

There is no GPS gap rule issue, but the underlying 12:16:50–12:25:20 stationary block (F3) covers the whole wait; if the rider shows the app never displayed the arrival/notification, she may argue she had no chance to come out, relying on the absence of a rider-side acceptance record rather than any system fact.

F17 records 2 previously upheld no-show disputes against this driver in 90 days, which the rider will use to argue a pattern of premature driver cancellations even though the policy treats profile facts as non-decisive and RD-6 does not apply to no-show cases.

points.response: Conceded as to mechanics: F6 (tap 12:17:10, 39 m) and F5 (platform-recorded arrival 12:15:25) do establish the driver's position at the tap, so NS-1(i)-(ii) is satisfied — but that only opens NS-1, it does not settle which fee was lawfully chargeable. Note also that under NS-1 the arrival confirmation here is a driver tap, not a platform auto-determination, and that distinction must be recorded as such.

This claim mislabels the money: the fee on record is $5.00 (F4, F7), which is the waiting-time fee figure, not the $6.61 cancellation fee, and NS-6 allows $5.00 only where the driver pressed "I'm Here", waited over 3 minutes, the rider boarded and the trip was completed with the fee tapped at drop-off — the driver cancelled and no trip was completed, so the $5.00 cannot stand however long he waited.

F3 and F1 show the driver stationary at the pickup for 8 min 30 s, which I do not dispute; but physical waiting is only a precondition, and NS-6 still requires the rider to have boarded and the journey to have completed (which F4 refutes), so this fact does not save the $5.00.

F9 and F11 show a complete, timestamped chat, and I rely on exactly those records: F10 (12:25, "8 min up, cancelling the trip") is the first and only notice of a no-show countdown, sent at the same minute as the cancellation, so no usable opportunity to board was ever given before the driver cancelled.

This claim concedes the decisive point: F7 shows the only sum billed is $5.00, so the driver cannot rely on the $6.61 cancellation fee under NS-1 and must instead satisfy NS-6, whose completion and drop-off-tap elements are absent (F4); with no completed trip there is no published basis for any charge, and FARE-1 requires the item to be returned.

Not in dispute and not relevant: no incident on the route (F14) and band 3 traffic (F13) with fair weather (F15) concern route-deviation justification under RD-4, and nothing in my case alleges a route deviation; these facts neither establish nor defend a $5.00 fee which the driver never earned by completing a trip.

I do not ask the panel to decide the fee on profile at all: F17 is offered only as a supporting basis for an account-review flag if my C2/C3/C6 succeed, since it records 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days against 824 trips — a pattern of the same conduct now alleged, and NS-2 expressly attaches a flag where the cancellation charge was not properly made out.

My own claim needs no repair but I sharpen it: because F7 shows $5.00 rather than $6.61, the driver's entire NS-1 argument (D1–D2) wins him the wrong fee — NS-1 can only sustain $6.61, so on his own facts nothing was chargeable and my requested $5.00 refund_full stands.
Conceded: F6, F4 and F5 establish that the "I'm Here" tap and the continuous wait were satisfied, so C1's factual reading in the driver's favour stands.

C2 mislabels the figure: the $5.00 on record is the no-show cancellation fee in this case — the timeline entry for the driver's cancellation at 12:25:20 records the cancellation fee as $5.00 (F4) and the fare record shows the same $5.00 as the only fee (F7), while nothing in the record shows a completed trip or a waiting-fee tap; NS-0 routes a driver-cancelled, rider-no-show case to NS-1, not to NS-6.

NS-6 is not engaged at all: it governs a waiting fee charged at drop-off after a completed trip, whereas this trip ended in a driver cancellation, so the charge is assessed under NS-1 and the absence of a drop-off tap is irrelevant rather than fatal (F4, F7).

The driver gave the rider the whole waiting window: he sent a time-stamped message identifying himself and the vehicle at the pickup at 12:17 (F9), stayed stationary 41 m away until 12:25:20 (F3, F2), and warned the rider immediately before cancelling (F10) — the record contains no rider message or GPS fact showing she ever reached the pickup point.

NS-2 does not apply because no NS-1 element failed: the tap was made by the driver at the pickup (F6), the platform arrival was recorded at 12:15:25 (F5), and the driver waited 8 min 10 s inside the radius after the tap (F6), so the fee stands and no refund is due.

An account flag is not a remedy and no NS-2 breach exists to support one; the driver's record also shows 824 trips in 90 days and a 3.2-year account (F17), against the rider's own profile of 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F16), so the profile facts do not tip this case.

notices.text: We looked at your dispute about the $5.00 cancellation charge and the driver's no-show report. The driver's arrival was recorded at the pickup, he stayed inside the pickup area for more than the 8-minute wait window, and he cancelled only after that window closed. So the $5.00 fee stands, and no refund is due. There is no change to your account, and no further action is needed from you.

We reviewed the no-show cancellation you reported for the $5.00 fee. Your arrival tap was recorded at the pickup, your location stayed inside the pickup area for the full required wait window, and the trip was cancelled only after that window closed. The $5.00 no-show fee is upheld and will be paid to you as a Ryde voucher. No action is being taken on your account.
